body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a frightening one out near Tehachapi, where agents working a train burglary came under fire overnight — deputies spent the small hours searching for a suspect who ran from the scene. Closer to home, expect a mild Friday, high near 72, air quality sitting at a healthy 35, and a Lake Wind Advisory in effect through tomorrow morning. Here's what happened while you slept.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came at 10:49 p.m., when deputies were sent to the railroad northeast of Woodford, near Tehachapi, after agents working an interrupted burglary of a train container reported that people inside the container shot at them. Two agents were reported not to be hurt and took cover behind their vehicles. Units staged about a half mile out and worked out access from the Highway 58 side and off Woodford and Keene. Deputies were told one suspect was believed to have fled south and then southwest, with no description available, and crews asked a hospital to confirm there were no gunshot victims. The railroad was cleared to resume traffic about 4 a.m. The only other gunfire calls of the night came at 6:05 a.m., when officers took about four reports of shots heard in the area of Morrill Avenue and Airport Drive.

Weapons calls were the other thread through the evening. Officers were sent at 7:04 p.m. to the 2,700 block of Ming Avenue for a robbery that had just happened at a clothing store, where a man in a ski mask took merchandise and left eastbound in a white sedan. Officers were sent into the 10th Street area at 8:14 p.m. for a domestic argument where the other person in the home was reported to have a firearm, and a roommate was reported to have threatened to shoot the person who called. Deputies were sent at 7:14 p.m. to the 8,400 block of Panama Road for a report of a man with a kitchen knife; he was reported to be inside the residence and no longer holding it.

Fire crews worked four structure fires through the night, starting at 7:31 p.m. on Ledgeview Lane in southwest Bakersfield. The last was an apartment on the 2,200 block of Nelson Street at 10:31 p.m. Deputies and fire crews searched the south side for a possible drowning at 3:18 a.m., and medics were sent at 4:12 a.m. to the 900 block of Olive Drive for a 2-year-old reported not to be breathing.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 72 degrees and a low around 51 tonight. It's currently 61 at Meadows Field. The National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a Lake Wind Advisory running until 10 a.m. Saturday, so if you're headed out to the lake or anywhere exposed, plan for gusty conditions. Air quality is good, with an AQI of 35, and there are no active fires reported in the county this morning. A mild, clear Friday — a good one to get outside before the wind picks up.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield Now reports that the City of Bakersfield is explaining why the Stockdale Highway off-ramp is closing permanently.** The city has laid out its reasoning for the closure, which will change how drivers move through one of the busiest corridors on the west side. If Stockdale is part of your commute, it's worth reading the city's explanation in full before the change takes hold.

**According to 23ABC, rising credit card debt is putting real pressure on Kern County households as everyday expenses climb.** Americans are holding nearly $1.3 trillion in credit card debt, per the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, and for some local residents cards have become a way to cover basic necessities when income doesn't stretch far enough. Arvin resident Reynalda Maldonado told the station that steady work is hard to find close to home and that a temporary job helped her pay down her balance — until the assignment ended and she was relying on credit again for rent, car bills, gas and food. CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart said wages aren't keeping up with inflation, and that higher-poverty areas like Kern County feel it more sharply.

**KGET 17 reports that a Bakersfield woman is describing an emergency landing after a pipe burst mid-flight.** She told the station it "just started rushing water down the aisle," an account that captures how quickly a routine trip turned into something else entirely. It's the kind of story that reminds you how much trust we place in the systems around us every time we buckle in.

**23ABC reports that Kern County is asking residents to prepare for El Niño.** Fire Captain Andrew Freeborn said there's a greater chance of a wetter-than-normal winter and that the county isn't going to take any chances — every department, including Fire, the Sheriff's Office and Public Works, is working together on readiness. Preparedness information is posted online, including sandpile locations where residents can fill sandbags for free, a winter checklist, a suggested go-bag inventory and emergency instructions. Freeborn urged residents to download the ReadyKern app, know their zone and learn their evacuation routes. A Public Works official added a simple reminder: mind the road signs — if they're up, they're there to keep you out and keep you safe.

**23ABC reports that a Bakersfield man convicted of killing Taylor Denay Dominguez was sentenced Thursday to 30 years to life in prison, plus an additional 10 years and four months.** Rafael Estrada pleaded no contest to second-degree murder in Dominguez's May 2025 death. At the sentencing, her family addressed the court, describing a lifetime of missing someone they'll never get back — "Taylor's life was never yours to take," one family member said — and urging others experiencing domestic violence to seek help. According to the family, Dominguez and her four children had moved in with her mother to escape what they described as an abusive relationship with Estrada; police say he later found them at the home on Monterey Street and, following an argument, stabbed Dominguez in the throat in front of two of her four children. Estrada expressed remorse and told the court he hopes to be forgiven one day.

**KGET 17 reports that body camera footage of a Bakersfield police shooting is raising serious questions.** The footage has prompted scrutiny of the encounter, and it's the kind of review that matters to public trust in how force is used here at home.

## Something good

Kern County has a gold medalist. A local parafencer won gold in international competition in Brazil, and has now set a goal of competing at the 2028 Paralympic Games. That's a long road from here to Los Angeles, and it starts with mornings like this one — so keep an eye on this athlete. We'd love to see a Kern County name on that stage.

## Coming up this week

A busy stretch of public meetings gets underway today. The Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee meets at noon, and if you've got thoughts on the look and care of your neighborhood, that's the room for them. Tuesday brings two: the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2 p.m. and the Historic Preservation Commission at 4 p.m. Wednesday is the heavy one — City Council meets in a pair of sessions, 3:30 p.m. and 5:15 p.m., so check the agenda for which items land where. Thursday, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m., and next Friday the Laws and Legislation Committee convenes at noon.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full calendar. Tonight, November 13, NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet takes the stage. Sunday, November 15 brings the 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards — a good night to celebrate the sound this town is known for. Later in the month: "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?" on November 23, Becky Robinson's Holiday Spectacular on November 27, and the Shrek Rave — Shrek The Halls — on December 4. Season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are also on sale.

Have a good Friday, Bakersfield. Watch for that wind, and we'll see you tomorrow.

top.title: The City of Bakersfield explains why Stockdale Highway off-ramp is closing permanently
